_about: Every word the analysis page shows that does not come from the run's payload: lending terms, section labels, and plain wording of legal concepts keyed by the model's node type. No party name, figure or case fact: {company} and {claimant} are filled from the payload's parties, figures from its data.

line.title: The line
line.limit_note: Slope's published sizing rule on the connected bank data

notes.due: Installments falling due by {horizon}, including the line's installments outstanding on the review date.
notes.past_due: Due by {horizon}, not collected and not frozen by a filing.
notes.stayed: Owed to Slope on the day of a bankruptcy filing, on outcomes with a filing by {horizon}; collection stops. It includes installments not yet due at the filing. Weighted over all outcomes (zero where no filing): {weighted}.
notes.not_yet_due: Installments falling due after {horizon}, on outcomes with no filing.
notes.filing: Share of outcomes in which {company} files, or is put into, bankruptcy by {horizon}.
notes.preference: Collections in the 90 days before a filing, which a trustee can seek to recover, on outcomes with a filing by {horizon}. Weighted over all outcomes (zero where no filing): {weighted}.
notes.unavailable: Not in this run's data yet.
notes.frozen_due: Due by {horizon} and not collected because a bankruptcy filing froze collection. Due = collected + past due + due, frozen by a filing.

forecast.chart: By month: funded, due and collected; outstanding at month end
forecast.assumptions_note: Settings every outcome shares. Section 5 switches one of them.
forecast.months_hover: {month}: funded {funded}, due {due}, collected {collected}; outstanding at month end {outstanding}

resolve.filing: Filing probability by {horizon}, given this outcome
resolve.follows: Most likely next (share of this outcome)
resolve.attribution_note: One forecast, read twice: with the lawsuit's cash effects, and with the lawsuit given no cash effect (the company's ordinary operating risk).
resolve.nothing: No further event in the period

judgment.jev: Jev is a forecasting model that reads the public record and gives the probability of one party's next move. Code sets every date and amount and combines the probabilities along each path.
judgment.question: Question
judgment.drag: Drag to override Jev's answer; every figure on the page follows.
judgment.why: Why this judgment: its answer moves expected collections most for how uncertain Jev is about it (the swing between 0% and 100%, weighted by Jev's uncertainty).
judgment.paths_note: The paths' first three events, sized by probability. Red: share of the path that ends in a filing by {horizon}.
judgment.tornado_note: Expected collections with each judgment set to 0% and 100% of the named answer. Jev's own answer is shown beside each swing.
judgment.paths_filing: Filing probability by {horizon} on this branch

assumption.shown: Compared below: the assumption with the largest combined move in filing probability and collection rate, in points.
assumption.path_note: The verdict table, the outcome grid and section 4 break down the central forecast; the other figures use the selected assumption.

actual.intro: Everything below happened after the review date; none of it was available to the forecast.
actual.filed: {company} filed for bankruptcy on {date}. The forecast put a filing by that date at {p}.
actual.filed_after: {company} filed for bankruptcy on {date}, after the period ended on {horizon}. The forecast put a filing by {horizon} at {p}.

judgment_response.question: Once judgment is entered, does {company} pay it, file for bankruptcy, or keep operating and contest it?

stay_motion.question: Does {company} ask the court to pause collection of the judgment against a bond or other security?

stay_approved.question: Does the court accept the offered security and pause collection?

registration_early.short: Court lets {claimant} collect in other states early

holders_act_judgment.question: Once the judgment default ripens, do the holders of 25% of the notes (or the trustee) give notice and demand repayment of the notes?
